title: Finite inner-horn filtration of paired-face join inclusions
statement: Use simplicial sets, standard simplices and horns from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and joins, pushouts and inner anodyne maps from [lem-coef-infinity-pushout-join-saturation]. Let $n\geq1$ and $0\leq k<n$. Let $J_n$ be the ordered set $\{\bar n<\cdots<\bar0<0<\cdots<n\}$, and identify its nerve with $\Delta^{2n+1}$. For a nonempty subset $S\subseteq J_n$, write $\Delta^S$ for its spanned face. Let $H_{n,k}\subseteq N(J_n)$ be the union of the two pure block faces $\Delta^{\{\bar n,\ldots,\bar0\}}$, $\Delta^{\{0,\ldots,n\}}$, and the faces $\Delta^{J_n\setminus\{\bar j,j\}}$ for all $0\leq j\leq n$ with $j\neq k$. There is a finite filtration $H_{n,k}=A_0\subseteq A_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq A_r=N(J_n)$ such that every inclusion $A_{a-1}\hookrightarrow A_a$ is a pushout of an inner horn inclusion $\Lambda^{d_a}_{e_a}\hookrightarrow\Delta^{d_a}$ with $d_a\geq2$ and $0<e_a<d_a$. In particular $H_{n,k}\hookrightarrow N(J_n)$ is inner anodyne.

source.place: Proposition 8.1.1.15, proof: finite filtration by primary and secondary subsets. Its parameter i is n-k in this statement. Kerodon tag 03JT, not a Stacks tag. Online source read; archival source WANTED.

proof.text: Reindex the ordered vertices of $J_n$ by the increasing bijection $\bar j\mapsto n-j$, $j\mapsto n+1+j$ onto $[2n+1]$. Put $i=n-k$, so $1\le i\le n$, and $h=2n+1-i$, so $n+1\le h<2n+1$. The deleted pair $\{\bar j,j\}$ becomes $\{t,2n+1-t\}$ with $t=n-j$. Call a nonempty subset $S\subseteq[2n+1]$ basic if (a) $S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n\}$, (b) $S\subseteq\{n+1,\ldots,2n+1\}$, or (c) it misses $\{t,2n+1-t\}$ for some $0\le t\le n$, $t\ne i$. Thus its spanned simplex lies in $H_{n,k}$ exactly when $S$ is basic. This follows directly from the faces defining $H_{n,k}$. More generally a simplex $f:[m]\to[2n+1]$ of any simplicial subset belongs to it exactly when the increasing simplex on its image belongs: factor $f$ as the surjection onto its ordered image followed by that image's inclusion; the surjection has a monotone section, obtained by choosing the first occurrence of each value. Precomposition with these maps proves both implications. Hence every subsequent membership calculation reduces to subsets of the vertices, including degenerate simplices.

source.place: Proposition 8.1.1.15 proof, definition of basic subsets and identification of the lifting domain.

proof.text: Write $L=\{0,\ldots,i-1\}$. A non-basic set is primary if it misses $L$ and contains $h$; it is secondary if it meets $L$ and contains $i$. Enumerate all primary and secondary subsets as $S_1,\ldots,S_r$ in nondecreasing cardinality, putting primary sets before secondary sets when cardinalities agree; within each remaining tie choose any order. Define $K_q$ to be the union of $K_0=H_{n,k}$ with the faces spanned by $S_1,\ldots,S_q$. These are simplicial subsets, since each face consists of the monotone maps with image in its vertex set. There are finitely many subsets, so this is a finite filtration. The full vertex set is non-basic, meets $L$ because $i>0$, and contains $i$; hence it is secondary. It is uniquely largest in cardinality and appears last, giving $K_r=\Delta^{2n+1}$. Every non-basic subset is also covered directly: if it meets $L$, adjoining $i$ gives a secondary superset; otherwise adjoining $h$ gives a primary superset. A superset of a non-basic set cannot be basic, since the three basic conditions are closed under taking subsets.

source.place: Proposition 8.1.1.15 proof, primary/secondary subsets and their cardinality ordering.

proof.text: Fix a primary $S=S_q=\{j_0<\cdots<j_d\}$. Since $S$ is non-basic it has a lower-block vertex $v\le n$; since it misses $L$, $v\ge i$. It also contains $2n+1$: it must meet the pair $\{0,2n+1\}$, as $0\ne i$, while $0\notin S$. Thus $v<h<2n+1$ shows that the index $t$ of $h$ in $S$ satisfies $0<t<d$, in particular $d\ge2$. Deleting a vertex other than $h$ gives a basic set or a smaller primary set, so that face is in $K_{q-1}$. Put $F=S\setminus\{h\}$. It is not basic: it retains $v$ in the lower block and $2n+1$ in the upper block, and deleting $h$ changes none of the required pair intersections, since $h$ belongs only to the excluded pair $\{i,h\}$. It is not primary (it lacks $h$) or secondary (it misses $L$). If $F$ lay in $K_{q-1}$, it would therefore be contained in a previous primary or secondary set $T$. Since $F$ is not of either type, $|T|>|F|=|S|-1$, whereas the ordering gives $|T|\le|S|$. Thus $|T|=|S|$. The primary-before-secondary rule forces $T$ to be primary; hence $F\cup\{h\}=S\subseteq T$, forcing $T=S$, contrary to being earlier. This proves that precisely the distinguished codimension-one face is absent at this stage.

source.place: Proposition 8.1.1.15 proof, primary case and the missing distinguished face.

proof.text: Fix a secondary $S=S_q=\{j_0<\cdots<j_d\}$. It contains a vertex $v<i$ and an upper-block vertex $w\ge n+1$, since it is non-basic. Hence $v<i<w$, and the index $t$ of $i$ satisfies $0<t<d$, so $d\ge2$. On deleting a vertex other than $i$, the remaining $S'$ contains $i$. If it is basic, it is in $K_0$. If it is non-basic and meets $L$, it is a smaller secondary set. If it is non-basic and misses $L$, $T=S'\cup\{h\}$ is a primary superset, has cardinality at most $|S|$, and is earlier by cardinality and the primary-before-secondary rule. In all three cases the deleted face is in $K_{q-1}$. Now $F=S\setminus\{i\}$ retains $v<i$ and the upper vertex $w$, and deleting $i$ changes no required pair intersection, since its pair is the excluded $\{i,h\}$. Therefore $F$ is non-basic; it is not primary because it meets $L$, and not secondary because it lacks $i$. If $F$ were contained in an earlier listed set $T$, then $|S|-1<|T|\le|S|$, so $|T|=|S|$. Since $T$ contains $v\in L$, it is secondary, hence contains $i$. Thus $S=F\cup\{i\}\subseteq T$, forcing $S=T$, a contradiction. Again precisely the distinguished codimension-one face is absent.

source.place: Proposition 8.1.1.15 proof, secondary case and the missing distinguished face.

proof.text: Let $S=S_q$ and let $u$ be its distinguished vertex ($h$ for primary sets, $i$ for secondary sets). Steps 3 and 4 put every face deleting $j\ne u$ in $K_{q-1}$ and exclude $F=S\setminus\{u\}$. They also exclude $S$, since a simplicial subset containing $S$ contains $F$. Every proper subset $U\subsetneq S$ other than $F$ omits some $j\ne u$ and lies in the corresponding already present face: if it omitted no such $j$, it would contain $F$, and the only possibilities would be $F$ and $S$. With the support criterion of step 1 this proves, in every simplicial degree, that the inverse image of $K_{q-1}$ under the increasing injection $\sigma_S:\Delta^d\to\Delta^{2n+1}$ is exactly $\Lambda_t^d$. Here $t$ is the index of $u$, and steps 3 and 4 give $0<t<d$.

source.place: Proposition 8.1.1.15 proof, identification of the inverse image L with an inner horn; explicit support argument.

proof.text: For the pushout assertion, maps $a:K_{q-1}\to X$ and $b:\Delta^d\to X$ agreeing on $\Lambda_t^d$ extend uniquely to $K_q=K_{q-1}\cup\sigma_S(\Delta^d)$: in each degree use $a$ on the first part and $b\circ\sigma_S^{-1}$ on the second. The injection $\sigma_S$ and the intersection calculation in step 5 make this well-defined, and restriction along every monotone map commutes with the two formulas because $a$ and $b$ are simplicial. Uniqueness holds on each part. This is precisely the universal property of the pushout of $\Lambda_t^d\hookrightarrow\Delta^d$ along its map to $K_{q-1}$; no general colimit theorem is being invoked. Set $A_q=K_q$ to obtain the asserted finite filtration, with $d_q=d$ and $e_q=t$ at each stage.

source.place: Proposition 8.1.1.15 proof, pushout square; degreewise proof of the elementary union gluing used there.

proof.text: By the definition in [lem-coef-infinity-pushout-join-saturation], each inner horn inclusion belongs to the inner anodyne class, and that class is closed under pushouts and transfinite compositions. Step 6 therefore puts each $K_{q-1}\hookrightarrow K_q$ in that class. Composing the finite chain is the special case indexed by the finite ordinal $r+1$ of transfinite composition (there are no nonzero limit stages to check). Hence $H_{n,k}=K_0\hookrightarrow K_r=N(J_n)$ is inner anodyne.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q20-69e0e1900 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read all of the mathematics. The statement matches Kerodon 03JT (Prop 8.1.1.15, proof read online): Kerodon's 0<i<=n with horn Lambda^n_{n-i} is the item's k=n-i, so n>=1 and 0<=k<n. After the reindexing bar j->n-j, j->n+1+j, the excluded pair becomes t=i, so H_{n,k} is exactly Kerodon's K_0, which is the lifting domain used in step 2 of the parent lem-coef-twisted-arrow-left-fibration (d_j of Tw deletes bar j and j). I re-derived each step. Step 1: the support criterion follows from a monotone section of the surjection. Step 2: every non-basic set has a primary or secondary superset, and the full set is secondary because 0 is in L. Step 3 (primary): 2n+1 is in S because the pair {0,2n+1} has t=0, which is not i, and 0 is not in S; so v<h<2n+1. Step 3 and step 4 (secondary): F is non-basic because the deleted vertex lies only in the excluded pair {i,h}, and an earlier set of equal size containing F is forced by the tie rule to equal S. Step 4 also covers a facet that loses L by adding h, giving an earlier primary set. Step 5: the inverse image is exactly the inner horn in every degree. Step 6: the pushout is a direct degreewise gluing. Step 7 uses only the defining sentence of lem-coef-infinity-pushout-join-saturation, which is in the same unit, so no tool_use is needed. My own brute force (/tmp/q20check/chk.py) passes all 15 cases with 1<=n<=5 and 0<=k<n, 3252 attachments in total, with the horn intersections and final coverage exact. In the edge case n=1, k=0, H is the spine of Delta^3, attached in 4 steps. The report's prose for this case leaves out the two middle 2-simplices; that slip is in the report only, not the node. Other checks: there are no new nodes, the dependency closure has no cycle, rg searches of the DAG for 03JT, twisted arrow, paired, edgewise and inner anodyne found no duplicate (so same_as=[] is right), all three Mathlib search kinds are recorded, and nothing cites SGA.
